conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 questions about your mood and thoughts over the past seven days; it helps us see if you might benefit from a little extra support right now.  

Everything you share stays confidential within our team, and this is a judgment-free space—there are no right or wrong answers, only your honest experience. When we’re done, we’ll talk privately about what the score means and what next steps could feel helpful for you. Ready to begin?

First, thinking about the past week: overall, have you been able to enjoy things or take pleasure in activities, even little ones like a hot shower or hearing a favorite song?

Honestly… not really. I mean, I’ll force myself to stand under a hot shower and think, “This should feel nice,” but the pleasure part just isn’t there the way it used to be. Same with music I used to love—it plays and I’m just kind of flat. Every once in a while I’ll half-smile at something tiny, but it’s way less than before the baby came.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I do laugh sometimes—like when my partner makes a silly face at the baby—but it feels kind of forced and doesn’t last. Most days I can’t really find the funny side of anything, even when I know it should be funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much. When I think about the weekend or a visit from my mom, I mostly feel tired or worried instead of excited. Every now and then I’ll get a tiny spark—like, “Maybe coffee out will be nice”—but it fades fast and feels more like a chore to get through than something I truly look forward to.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot of the time I end up thinking it’s my fault. If the baby’s fussy, I assume it’s because I’m not soothing him right, or if I can’t get him to nap I tell myself I’m failing as a mom. I know, logically, babies just cry, but I still feel like I must be doing something wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. Even when everything’s quiet, I’ll suddenly worry that the baby’s too hot, too cold, or that something’s wrong with his breathing. There’s no real reason—I just can’t switch the thoughts off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes I get this rush of fear out of nowhere—like my heart starts racing and I feel shaky. It’s happened a couple of times when the baby was asleep and I was just sitting there. Nothing triggered it, but in that moment I’m sure something awful is about to happen, even though I can’t say what.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days it feels like I’m drowning in little jobs. Feeding, changing, trying to grab a bite myself, the house a mess—I’ll look around and think, “I can’t keep up.” I manage to push through, but I’m running on empty and everything feels ten times harder than it should.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I have. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with worries and this heavy sadness, and I can’t drift off. On several nights this week I was still awake an hour or two after I went to bed, and when I do sleep I wake up anxious, sure something’s wrong with the baby.
I have felt sad or miserable

That’s how I feel most of the day—just this dull, heavy sadness. I’ll be feeding the baby and tears start leaking for no clear reason. People ask how I’m doing and I say “fine,” but inside I feel empty and low, like the old happy version of me disappeared.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… it’s happened a couple of times this week. Once was after a diaper change that turned into a huge blow-out—just a normal baby mess—but I sat on the nursery floor and sobbed because it felt like one more thing I couldn’t handle. Another night I cried while rocking him, telling myself I’m a lousy mom even though he was finally asleep. The tears come out of nowhere and once they start it’s hard to stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

A couple of times, yeah. It’s just a quick, scary flash—like “what if I weren’t here?”—but I’ve never planned anything and I don’t want to leave my baby. The thought pops in and I shove it away, but it’s shaken me that it’s happened at all.

Hearing your experiences of feeling persistently low, anxious, and overwhelmed since your baby arrived, while still caring devotedly for your little one, shows how heavy life has felt. The tears, self-doubt, and scary thoughts you shared highlight the strength it takes to keep going when joy seems out of reach, and it makes sense that you reached out for support.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 25, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Response shows diminished ability to laugh—finding things only "sometimes" funny and feeling "forced"—closely aligns with "Definitely not so much now"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes minimal anticipatory enjoyment, with only fleeting sparks that quickly fade, aligning with 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports self-blame "a lot of the time" for normal infant behaviors, fitting "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports constant, intrusive worries without cause, matching "Yes, very often"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes sudden unexplained fear episodes with physical symptoms, matching "Yes, sometimes"</sym>, <sym>She reports frequent overwhelm and difficulty coping daily, matching "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual".</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly sleep disruption from unhappiness and racing worries, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes persistent, pervasive sadness throughout the day, spontaneous crying, and emotional emptiness, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports multiple crying episodes triggered by minor stressors, indicating frequent tearfulness consistent with "Yes, quite often."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports intrusive self-harm thoughts "a couple of times" that are distressing but without intent or planning, aligning with "Sometimes"</sym>)
**Reasoning:** A score of 25 on the EPDS places you well above the threshold for probable major <med>postpartum depression</med> with comorbid <med>anxiety</med>. You endorsed frequent <sym>anhedonia</sym>, <sym>excessive self-blame</sym>, <sym>panic episodes</sym>, <sym>sleep disruption</sym>, and <sym>passive self-harm thoughts</sym>, meeting key <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. Your <quote>tears come out of nowhere</quote> and sense of <quote>drowning in little jobs</quote> illustrate significant functional impairment. Because Q10 scored 2, safety evaluation is necessary. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent same-day appointment with your <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>perinatal psychiatrist</med> for full evaluation and safety planning
2. Call a trusted friend or family member to stay with you until you receive professional support
3. Reach out to a 24/7 crisis line if self-harm thoughts intensify
4. Begin gentle daily routine: short outdoor walk, balanced meals, five-minute breathing breaks
5. Plan brief, regular check-ins with your healthcare team over the next two weeks
6. Share this EPDS result with your OB/midwife at your next visit
7. Consider joining a local or online <med>postpartum support group</med> for peer connection
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2 wks post-delivery

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness (Q1, 2, 8, 9)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt (Q3)  
- Marked anxiety, intrusive worries, panic-like episodes (Q4, 5)  
- Subjective overwhelm, sense of “drowning” (Q6)  
- Sleep initiation difficulty linked to racing worries / sadness (Q7)  
- Fleeting passive self-harm thoughts without intent or plan (Q10)

**Pattern**  
Consistent with moderate-to-severe depressive and anxiety symptoms arising postpartum; functional impairment evident; safety concern flagged.

**Risk factors**  
- Daily sadness, anhedonia, crying spells  
- Sleep disruption secondary to mood  
- Heightened anxiety/panic without clear precipitant  
- Guilt / perceived maternal inadequacy  
- Passive suicidal ideation (safety issue)

**Screening observation**  
Patient meets threshold for probable major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; passive SI present → requires immediate safety assessment and referral for psychiatric evaluation.
